text:
Quantitative survey of obstetric anesthesia practices among physicians across Arab countries, describing process indicators, protocols, and perioperative routines. It reports practice patterns (what respondents do), not prescriptive recommendations.

Labor analgesia. Epidural analgesia was the primary technique, reported by 83% of respondents. Regarding timing, 90% administered the epidural before reaching 5 cm of cervical dilation or irrespective of dilation achieved. For high-risk pregnancies, 37% reported placing preemptive early epidural catheters.

Anesthesia for cesarean delivery. The reported cesarean delivery rate was 31-50% among 46% of respondents. The primary anesthetic technique was spinal anesthesia, reported by 98% of respondents. Intrathecal morphine for post-cesarean analgesia was used by 39%. Aspiration prophylaxis when performing general anesthesia for cesarean delivery was used by 54%. Prophylactic antibiotics were administered only after umbilical cord clamping by just 20%.

Management of spinal-induced hypotension. Approaches varied widely across respondents; only 15% reported using a prophylactic phenylephrine infusion, indicating that vasopressor prophylaxis is not yet routine in the surveyed practice.

Pre-anesthesia screening. For epidural and spinal anesthesia respectively, 63% and 68% required prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time and INR from patients without a history of hemorrhagic complications, while 93% and 88% required a platelet count.

Systems and education. Written departmental protocols existed in variable proportions across areas. Regular meetings to discuss complications were held by 81%, presentations on obstetric anesthesia topics by 73%, and 51% conducted research in the field.

Relevance. This survey maps real-world obstetric anesthesia practice in Arab countries, useful context for a practice operating in the region. Because it is a self-reported survey, the percentages describe reported practice and should not be read as evidence-based targets.
title: Insights into obstetric anesthesia practices: a quantitative survey among physicians across Arab countries
